newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sees 1997 inflation lower than '96 3.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sees 1997 inflation lower than '96 3.4 pct.

text.p: Croatia's 1997 retail price inflation could be cut below the 3.4 percent recorded at the end of last year and from 3.7 percent in 1995, Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro said on Monday.
"The 1997 target is even lower inflation...and our low consolidated budget deficit is the best guarantee for this," Skegro told a news conference.

The deficit of nearly 40 billion kuna for the central budget and extrabudgetary institutions, including the health and pension funds, was projected at under 3.0 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) this year.
According to the latest set of official statistics, December retail prices were at a standstill after rising 0.5 percent in November. They rose 3.4 percent from December 1995.
The annualised 1996 inflation was 3.5 percent on average compared to the previous year.
Skegro said it translated into an average 0.3 percent for the past three years as Croatia experienced a 3.0 percent retail price decline in 1994 and a 5.5 drop in producer prices.
This was a result of a "careful government programme rather than mere chance" since it launched stiff measures to stabilise the economy in October 1993, he said.
Inflation measured by producer prices was 1.5 percent in December last year compared to the same month of 1995. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
